question: Simplify: sqrt{51 - sqrt{7 + sqrt{11 - 4sqrt{7}}}}
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Start with the innermost square root: √(11 − 4√7) = √(√7 − 2)² = √7 − 2.

Substitute this value back into the intended expression: √(51 − √7 + √7 − 2).

The irrational terms −√7 and +√7 cancel each other out perfectly.

This simplifies the remaining expression to: √(51 − 2) = √49.

Finally, the square root of 49 is 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: √(51 − √7 + √(11 − 4√7))

**Formula Used:**

(a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab

**Calculation:**

⇒ First, evaluate the innermost radical: √(11 − 4√7)

⇒ The term inside can be rewritten as: 11 − 4√7 = 7 + 4 − 2 × 2 × √7

⇒ Applying the algebraic identity, we get: (√7)² + (2)² − 2 × √7 × 2

⇒ This perfectly forms a square: (√7 − 2)²

⇒ Therefore, the square root simplifies to: √(√7 − 2)² = √7 − 2

⇒ Now, substitute this result into the complete expression:

⇒ √(51 − √7 + √7 − 2)

⇒ The −√7 and +√7 terms offset and cancel each other out.

⇒ The expression now becomes: √(51 − 2)

⇒ √49

⇒ 7

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simplifying Surds of the Form √(a ± √b)

To simplify such surds, we convert the inner expression into a perfect square (x ± y)² = x² + y² ± 2xy, where the rational part equals x² + y² and the irrational part matches 2xy.

Addition and Subtraction of Surds

Only like surds (surds having the same index and same radicand) can be added or subtracted. For example, m√x ± n√x = (m ± n)√x.

Nested Radicals and BODMAS

When solving expressions with nested radicals, always begin simplification from the innermost radical and work your way outward step by step.
